title: Andrej Karpathy: Software Is Changing (Again)
summary: Karpathy's 'Software Is Changing (Again)': Software 3.0, LLMs as fallible 'people spirits', partial autonomy, keeping AI on a leash, building docs for agents.

assertions.quote: your prompts are now programs that program the LLM ... these prompts are written in English

verdicts.note: A framing of how software is built rather than a testable factual claim; widely adopted as a lens.

Many sources frame vibe coding as a new paradigm with natural language as the primary interface (67% of 36 RQ1 sources use an NL-to-code framing); this reflects how it is framed, not a demonstrated paradigm shift.

assertions.quote: They display jagged intelligence ... they will insist that 9.11 is greater than 9.9

verdicts.note: Well documented: uneven performance across tasks, persistent simple failures alongside expert-level output.

assertions.quote: it's less Iron Man robots and more Iron Man suits that you want to build

verdicts.note: Matches 2025-26 usage patterns (interactive agents dominate), though fully autonomous background agents have grown useful for scoped tasks.
The review names a tension between agentic delegation framings and the most-recommended safeguards (HITL review, validation), concluding 'a workable balance appears to lie between the two'.

assertions.quote: we as humans are doing the verification. It is in our interest to make this loop go as fast as possible

verdicts.note: Review is the measured bottleneck (DORA, Faros); tooling that speeds verification directly addresses it.

assertions.quote: I always go in small incremental chunks

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: it's not useful to me to get a diff of 10,000 lines of code to my repo ... I'm still the bottleneck

verdicts.note: The SmartBear/Cisco review study found defect detection drops beyond ~200-400 LOC per session; AI makes large PRs cheap to produce.
The vibe-coding review names a verification gap between generation speed and developers' capacity to verify. It doesn't measure PR size.

assertions.quote: spend a bit more time to be more concrete in your prompts which increases the probability of successful verification

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: when I see things like oh 2025 is the year of agents I get very concerned ... this is the decade of agents

verdicts.note: A long-range forecast; consistent with autonomy history (self-driving) but not yet checkable.

assertions.quote: the code was actually the easy part ... most of it actually was when I tried to make it real

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.
The 47-source review finds evidence strongest for prototyping and UI work and weakest for production. The break-down half is mostly unstudied, not shown.

assertions.quote: I had the menu genen basically demo working on my laptop in a few hours and then it took me a week

verdicts.note: Widely observed and consistent with Stanford's rework data and METR; the exact 70/30 split is a heuristic.

assertions.quote: Vercel ... is replacing every occurrence of click with an equivalent curl command

verdicts.note: Agents parse markdown and commands far more reliably than GUI instructions; llms.txt and markdown docs are spreading for this reason.

assertions.quote: they are susceptible to prompt injection risks. They might leak your data

verdicts.note: Repeatedly demonstrated against coding agents (malicious repos, issues, docs and MCP tool descriptions causing exfiltration or unsafe commands).

assertions.quote: suddenly everyone is a programmer because everyone speaks natural language

verdicts.note: Tools like Lovable, v0, Replit let non-developers produce working prototypes; widely observed.
45% of sources stress accessibility for novices and non-programmers. That evidence is mostly grey literature and centered on prototypes.
